name: United States

format.notes: An officer asks up to 20 questions from the published list of 128 and stops once 12 are answered correctly or 9 incorrectly. Applies to Form N-400 filed on or after 20 October 2025; earlier filers take the 2008 test.

exemptions.age: Applicants aged 65 or over with at least 20 years as a permanent resident get special consideration: a marked subset of the questions. Those 50 or over with 20 years’ residence (and a similar older rule) are excused from the English requirement.
exemptions.disability: An exception to the English and civics requirements is available for a physical or developmental disability or mental impairment; accommodations are also provided.

unverified.regional_variants: Not read. Some answers on the list (such as the applicant’s own senators or governor) depend on where the applicant lives.
unverified.fee: No separate test fee is described; the cost is the N-400 filing fee, which was not read.

recent_change.summary: The 2025 civics test replaced the 2008 one for applications filed on or after 20 October 2025: 128 questions on the list, up to 20 asked, 12 needed.

notes: The whole question list is published by the agency. Works of the United States government are generally in the public domain, but the agency’s own copyright page could not be opened here, so the licence is left unconfirmed. A separate English test (reading, writing, speaking) is part of the same interview.
